segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he kept back some of the price for himself, with his wife fully aware of it, and he brought just a part and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back for yourself some of the price of the land?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: While it remained unsold, did it not remain yours? And once it was sold, was it not at your disposal? Why is it that you set this deed in your heart? You have not lied to people but to God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came on all who heard of it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The younger men got up, wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After an interval of about three hours his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter addressed her:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Tell me, did you two sell the land for this much?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Yes, for that much.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Peter said to her,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why is it that you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And great fear came on the whole assembly and on all who heard of these things.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were taking place among the people. And they were all together, with one mind, in Solomon’s Colonnade.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: None of the rest dared to join them, but the people held them in high honor,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all the more, believers in the Lord were being added, multitudes of both men and women,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that people even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that as Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The multitude from the towns around Jerusalem also kept gathering, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the high priest rose up, and all who were with him, that is, the party of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they laid hands on the apostles and put them in public custody.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, led them out, and said,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Go, take your stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began teaching. When the high priest and those with him arrived, they called together the council, that is, the whole body of elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the jail to have them brought.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the officers arrived, they did not find them in the prison. They went back and reported,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We found the jail locked with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them we found no one inside.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were completely at a loss about them, wondering what this might lead to.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then someone arrived and reported to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, the men you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the captain went off with the officers and brought them, but not by force, for they were afraid of being stoned by the people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They brought them and stood them before the council. And the high priest questioned them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man’s blood on us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter and the apostles answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We must obey God rather than people.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: God exalted this man to his right hand as Leader and Savior, to give Israel turning back and forgiveness of sins.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this they were infuriated and wanted to kill them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But a Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law honored by all the people, stood up and ordered the men to be put outside for a little while.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Men of Israel, take care what you are about to do with these men.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, attached themselves to him. He was killed, and all who were persuaded by him were dispersed and came to nothing.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew people away after him. He too perished, and all who were persuaded by him were scattered.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So now I tell you, keep away from these men and leave them alone—because if this plan or this work is from people, it will be overthrown,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them—or you may even be found fighting against God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were persuaded by him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and after calling in the apostles they had them flogged, ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they went out from the presence of the council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to be dishonored for the sake of the Name.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that the Messiah is Jesus.

notes.phrase: kept back some of the price for himself
notes.traditional: kept back part of the price
notes.note: The verb means quietly setting aside for oneself what belongs to a common fund; in Titus 2:10 it describes pilfering. The Greek version of Joshua uses it for Achan's theft of goods devoted to God (Joshua 7:1), and many scholars think Luke intends the echo. As Peter says in verse 4, the offence is the deception, not the failure to give everything.

A first-century hearer knew this word as a civic gathering and as the Septuagint's term for Israel assembled before God. 'Church' is the near-universal rendering and readers know what it refers to, but it now suggests a building or an institution. This translation uses 'assembly' throughout so that the reader can see it is one Greek word.

It is disputed who 'the rest' are and what they did not dare to do. Most take them as outsiders who kept a respectful distance from the group in the colonnade, in contrast with those who came to believe (verse 14). Others take them as the other believers, who did not presume to stand alongside the apostles. The Greek does not settle it.

notes.phrase: believers in the Lord were being added
notes.traditional: believers were the more added to the Lord
notes.note: 'The Lord' can go with either word: 'those believing in the Lord were added' or 'believers were added to the Lord'. Both readings are grammatical and both are found in the major translations.

notes.phrase: that is, the whole body of elders
notes.note: The Greek has 'the council and the whole body of elders'. Most scholars take 'and' as explanatory, with the second phrase describing the council in the language the Septuagint uses for Israel's elders. The alternative reads two bodies, the council plus a wider gathering of elders.
The Greek word means human beings in general, not males. The contrast is between divine and human authority, and the same word is rendered 'people' in verses 4 and 38.

The word means wood or anything made of it: a tree, a pole, a beam. Here it refers to the cross. The phrasing echoes Deuteronomy 21:22–23, where a body hung on a tree is under God's curse, and 'tree' is kept so the echo can be heard.

'Repentance' now centres on feeling sorry. The Greek word carries the prophets' call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct. Most translations keep 'repentance' as an established term that readers understand to include a change of life.

notes.traditional: with his right hand / to his right hand
notes.note: The Greek can mean 'to his right hand', the place of honor, or 'by his right hand', the instrument of God's power. Translations are divided. The same phrase and the same ambiguity occur at Acts 2:33.

Josephus describes a Theudas who led a popular movement and was killed under the governor Fadus, around AD 44–46. That is later than the setting of this speech and later than Judas the Galilean (AD 6), whom Gamaliel places after him. Some conclude that Luke's chronology is mistaken here; others suppose an earlier, otherwise unknown Theudas. The question is unresolved.

This is the registration for taxation carried out in AD 6 under Quirinius, when Judea came under direct Roman rule. Josephus reports that Judas led resistance to it on the ground that submitting to Roman taxation was disloyalty to God.

The Greek has 'the Christ' with the article followed by 'Jesus'. In Acts this marks a title, and the claim being announced is that the expected Messiah is Jesus. Older versions render it as the name 'Jesus Christ'; several modern translations have 'Jesus is the Messiah' or 'Jesus as the Christ'.

candidates.reason: Translators split between 'council' and 'Sanhedrin' across the Gospels and Acts, and the reader should see one body named one way.
It occurs in Acts 3:15, 5:31 and Hebrews 2:10, 12:2 and is rendered variously as prince, author, pioneer, founder or leader; one decision is needed.
It is used of Sadducees, Pharisees and the Nazarenes in Acts and of factions in the letters; 'sect', 'party', 'faction' and 'heresy' carry very different tones.
It is a recurring Acts keyword for the community's unity, and also for hostile crowds, rendered variously as 'with one accord', 'together' or 'united'.
It is used of the cross in Acts 5:30, 10:39, 13:29, Galatians 3:13 and 1 Peter 2:24 with a Deuteronomy echo that 'cross' or 'wood' would hide, and of the tree of life in Revelation.
